findings: Equal-length rc.sysinit data replacement: drops the last two mount echo lines and appends a background Lua start after every mount; only the differing tail is stored.
The ROMFS inode checksum covers the unchanged 32-byte header/name and the filesystem checksum covers its unchanged first 512 bytes.
The AP header is version 0x00050000 with no signature block, and no AP-image integrity check was found in vela_bl2.bin strings. Physical boot acceptance is NOT verified.
The erase block also holds 1006 live bytes after the ROMFS: the NAND partition tables (resource / nand_data / coredump / nand_nv) and colour tables, one with pointers into this block.
MTD up_progmem_eraseblock (0xc19e7a4) erases inside BASEPRI 0x80, then always calls usleep(1) before FTL programs the block, so other tasks run while it is blank.

The Supervisor now erases and programs the whole block with the BES flash HAL (symbols flash.app_flash_erase/program/flush) inside one BASEPRI 0x80 section, after a bits-only probe of the dropped echo line; block states are identified by block_crc32; unpinning clears 's' of the hook to '#' without an erase. Emulator evidence only (scripts/emu/boot_smoke.py).

boot.lua runs under the firmware's NSH `lua`, whose luaopen_screen keeps the interpreter's lua_State in a three-slot table (symbol lua.screen_lua_states) for screen_state_cb; only the app framework's lua_module_miwear_close clears a slot, so the state stays there after `lua` exits and every later screen change runs lua_getglobal on freed memory. Mirage p67: slot 0 still holds the state of an exited `lua -e`. It did not fault there because the freed memory was not reused yet; on a band it can fault at any screen change after a pinned start. boot.lua (generated) now clears its own slot, matched against tostring(coroutine.running()), with one aligned `mw` write before anything else.
